Graph of the Outer Criterion Against a Hyperparameter

Source: R/plot_smooth.R
plot_criterion.Rd

Selects the graph of the outer criterion of the fit (the criterion that estimated the hyperparameters: reml(), ml(), aic() or bic()) as a function of the logarithm of one hyperparameter of a term, with the other hyperparameters held at their fitted values. The fitted value is marked, and the effective degrees of freedom of the term are drawn on a second axis.

Usage

plot_criterion(
  log_lambda = NULL,
  method = "refit",
  hyper = NULL,
  legend = TRUE
)

Arguments

log_lambda

NULL, or a numeric vector of values of the logarithm of the hyperparameter.

method

"refit" (the default) or "quadratic".

hyper

NULL, or the name of the hyperparameter of the term.

legend

Whether to draw the legend that names the elements of the graph.

Value

A PlotCriterion object, inheriting from term_plot.

Details

The hyperparameter is a smoothing parameter, the precision \(\lambda\) of a quadratic penalty, or the scale of a random effect, as the term names it (hyper selects it when the term has several). The horizontal axis is \(\log \theta\), with \(\theta\) the value of the hyperparameter, so that a hyperparameter whose value is not positive has no graph. The default grid has 41 points within five units of the fitted logarithm.

With method = "refit" the criterion is evaluated at each grid point exactly: the model is refitted with the hyperparameter at that value, the coefficients are warm-started at the fit, and the criterion is read at the refitted mode, as the outer search itself reads it. The effective degrees of freedom of the term are read at the same refit. The criterion that reml() and ml() estimate also estimates the coefficients of an equation for a dispersion (the sigma of a gaussian); these stay at their fitted values. With method = "quadratic" the criterion is the second-order expansion \(c(\eta_0) + g\,\delta - \tfrac{1}{2} A\,\delta^2\) in the free coordinate \(\eta = h(\theta)\), where \(h\) is the link of the hyperparameter, \(\delta = \eta - \eta_0\), \(g\) is the exact outer gradient and \(-A\) the exact diagonal element of the outer Hessian at the fit; it needs reml() or ml() and shows no degrees of freedom. The criterion is shown as the fit reports it (for reml() and ml() the log marginal likelihood, to be maximized; for aic() and bic() the criterion, to be minimized).

See also

plot_effect(), hyper()

Examples

set.seed(1)
dd <- data.frame(x = runif(120))
dd$y <- sin(2 * pi * dd$x) + rnorm(120, sd = 0.3)
fit <- statmod(y ~ s(x), distributions7::gaussian1_distrib(), dd)
ggplot2::autoplot(fit, term = "s(x)",
                  plot_type = plot_criterion(log_lambda = seq(-3, 8, length.out = 12)))
